_doc: Shot plan: one entry per timeline scene. motion = what is ON SCREEN as the primary visual (clip | film | graphic | parallax | kenburns | still | text); inserts = timed segments of another kind inside the scene. build:<id> = a procedural graphic drawn by build.py (no media file). planlint verifies motion against clips.json + media.json and measures static holds from the built timeline.

brand.fonts: Oswald, Anton, DM Serif, Special Elite
brand.title: red-band headline + paper kicker

fingerprint.hook_type: impossible-fact cold open (machines running with no power)
fingerprint.opening_shot: CU insert: hand lifting off a telegraph key, tape still feeding
fingerprint.first_line: In 1859, two telegraph operators unplugged their batteries… and kept on talking.
fingerprint.music: E minor, 72 bpm telegraph-sounder pulse, unresolved Esus2 ending
fingerprint.climax_device: night-side Earth globe under the closing warning line
fingerprint.structure: 10 scenes: anomaly → cause (flare) → arrival → effects ×3 → paradox → doubt → near miss → warning

shots.subject: telegraph key working by itself
shots.information_role: Hook: the impossible fact, a telegraph working with its battery disconnected, then the sky as the source.
shots.reason: Opens on the anomaly itself so the question lands before any context.

shots.subject: Carrington at Redhill and his drawing

inserts.label: his own drawing, A/B patches glow and travel to C/D

shots.information_role: Who saw the flare, where and when, shown with the primary evidence: Carrington's own drawing.
shots.reason: Real archive (engraving, photo, drawing) proves the date-and-time claim on screen.

shots.subject: solar flare footage
shots.information_role: The flare fades within sixty seconds and is gone in five minutes.
shots.reason: Real NASA SDO flare footage makes the brief event visible, labelled as illustrative.

shots.subject: magnetic storm and aurora
shots.information_role: Seventeen hours later the field trace goes wild and aurora reaches as far south as Cuba.
shots.reason: An animated trace turns an abstract storm into a visible event before the aurora footage.

shots.subject: campers under the aurora
shots.information_role: Human scale: campers thought the aurora was dawn and started breakfast.
shots.reason: The most relatable anecdote, from the Rocky Mountain News, animated as a living diorama.

shots.subject: telegraph office sparking
shots.information_role: Effects on the network: sparks, shocks, burning paper, lines unusable for hours.
shots.reason: Electric-arc overlays, flashes and a burn sell the danger on the office plate.

shots.subject: Boston to Portland line on auroral current
shots.information_role: Pays off the hook: operators disconnected batteries and worked about two hours on the auroral current.
shots.reason: Map, live-current pulse and the real transcript quote make the paradox concrete and sourced.

shots.subject: Carrington's caution
shots.information_role: Carrington refused to claim the flare caused the storm: one swallow does not make a summer.
shots.reason: His real portrait plus his own words give the scientific-humility beat weight.

shots.subject: July 2012 near miss

inserts.label: orbit diagram: STEREO-A hit, Earth missed, 1 week earlier

shots.information_role: A storm at least as strong crossed Earth's orbit in 2012; a week earlier it would have hit us.
shots.reason: Actual STEREO-A footage of the eruption, then a diagram explains why it missed.

shots.subject: Earth at night
shots.information_role: Stakes today: the next storm will find a world built on wires.
shots.reason: The lit night side shows how much now depends on the grid, closing on the warning line.
